scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported Air polygon and Sultanate of Agadez Wikipedia identity match the Aïr region. This is not the earlier state of Takedda or a claim to every Tuareg community.
Early fifteenth-century formation is approximate. The imported 1715 to 1815 map interval is not the state’s lifetime.

Cressier’s early architectural reconstruction and ICOMOS both recognize nineteenth-century work on the minaret; it is not presented as an untouched fifteenth-century monument. No oldest/tallest superlative is required.
The museum ornament comes from Azawagh and is twentieth century. It illustrates a named regional form, not an archaeological find at the sultan’s palace.
Baier’s accessible published extract was read; the full subscription article and its underlying archives were not claimed as inspected.
The 2025 restoration paper is used for its documented fieldwork. Its apparent population errors for Agadez and Niamey are omitted.
No map successor is linked without event-year geometry. Colonial subordination and continuing traditional institutions are distinguished.
UNESCO’s public listing and ICOMOS’s separately authored technical evaluation are distinct works; no passage is quoted verbatim. Independent historical and geographical review remains pending.
